<!-- Generated by Kora's design director. This is the design decision the site was built
     from. Business: JayaKrishna Arts -->

# DESIGN.md — JayaKrishna Arts

archetype: editorial-agency
rationale: With no photographs, no listed work and nothing beyond a name and a seven-word tagline, editorial-agency lets a business built on hand-painting argue through taste alone: poster-scale type and confident terracotta fields make a short page feel deliberate rather than unfinished.
interaction_level: L2

personality: [crafted, assured, warm, unhurried]

typography:
  display: "Instrument Sans"
  body: "Newsreader"
  scale: 1.414
  notes: Display is Instrument Sans at weight 600, tracked slightly tight (-0.02em). It is pushed to true poster scale in the hero, around clamp(3.5rem, 11vw, 10rem), so the business name and tagline become the visual subject in place of the paintings we cannot show. The step down is steep. Hero type is followed directly by a section heading at about 2.5rem, then the body. Newsreader body sits at 1.125rem with a 1.6 line-height and a measure of about 60ch. It is the long-hand, human counterweight to the sans, the way a painter's note sits beside the work. Small-caps eyebrows use Instrument Sans at 0.75rem, letter-spaced 0.14em, and are the only small type on the page. Nothing else is set small.

palette:
  primary: "#b8402a"
  secondary: "#f4efe6"
  accent: "#1c1a17"
  ground: "#f4efe6"
  surface: "#ebe3d6"
  ink: "#1c1a17"
  muted: "#6b5f55"
  border: "#d6cab9"
  application: |
    Primary terracotta works structurally across whole panels: the hero field, and the band behind the enquiry. It is never just a button colour.
    - Ground is the brand's own cream (secondary).
    - Ink is the brand's near-black (accent), which already carries a warm brown undertone.
    - Muted and border come from the same earth: a pigment-brown grey and a raw-linen hairline.
    The page reads like terracotta, chalk and lamp-black on unprimed canvas, the materials of a painter. That ties these neutrals to a hand-painting business and not to any brand that happens to use orange.
    Contrast pairs as shipped:
    - Cream on terracotta: about 4.8:1, safe for body and display.
    - Near-black on cream: about 15:1.
    - Muted on ground: about 5.4:1. Muted on surface: about 4.8:1.
    - Near-black on terracotta: about 3.1:1, so use it for large display type only, never body text.
    - Form inputs on the terracotta band take an explicit cream background (#f4efe6) and near-black text (#1c1a17), with the placeholder in muted (#6b5f55).

composition:
  whitespace: generous
  photography: none
  card_usage: none
  mobile: |
    - Hero type drops to about 3.25rem but stays dominant, and the tagline's two sentences stay on separate lines.
    - Any colour split in the hero stacks top to bottom instead of side to side, and it stays left-aligned rather than centred.
    - The enquiry form becomes a single full-width column with fields at least 48px tall.
    - No horizontal scroll and no sticky bar. There is one action on the page and it is never more than a scroll away.

composition: |
  The tagline is the entire argument. "Painted by hand. Kept for generations." makes two promises, one about the making and one about the lasting. Set them as the page's one unforgettable moment: enormous, asymmetric and off-balance, split across terracotta and cream like a canvas half-primed. Then offer a single way to begin a conversation.
  There is no list of work and no story to tell yet, so hold all of that back rather than pretend. The page is short and confident, and it ends on the enquiry.

sections:
  - id: hero
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: |
      Make the business name and the tagline, exactly as written, the distinctive moment the owner points at.
      "Painted by hand." and "Kept for generations." are the two halves of the case. They should feel weighted and permanent, with terracotta used as a painted field rather than decoration. A single quiet link leads down to the enquiry.
  - id: contact
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: |
      Give a visitor the one honest way to reach JayaKrishna Arts.
      Use an enquiry form with form_type "contact", posting to the Kora forms endpoint, with reCAPTCHA loaded lazily.
      It collects name, email and a message in the visitor's own words about what they are looking for. Do not suggest services or mediums the business has not named.
      The invitation should feel personal and unhurried, like writing to an artist rather than filing a ticket.
      No phone, email or address is shown, because none exists.

avoid:
  - Any phone number, email address, street address or map, including placeholder or "coming soon" versions. None are available.
  - Any services, mediums, price list, "what we paint" grid, or example subjects in form placeholders. The business has supplied none, and inventing "portraits / murals / canvases" would be fabrication.
  - A gallery, filmstrip or image placeholder of any kind, including grey boxes, blurred swatches pretending to be paintings, and stock or Unsplash art.
  - An invented about paragraph, founder story, founding year or "family tradition" narrative. The tagline is the only story given, and it must be quoted verbatim.
  - Clip-art paintbrushes, palette icons, SVG paint-splash flourishes or faux watercolour textures. These are the cliché of "art" sites. Here the type and the colour fields carry the craft.
  - Reviews, testimonial blocks, star ratings or "trusted by" lines.
  - Nav items for pages that do not exist (Gallery, About, Services, Prices). The nav carries only the name and a link to the enquiry.
  - A newsletter signup. It was not requested and there is nothing to send.
  - A centred hero over three cards, centred-everything symmetry, or any three-up icon row of "values".
  - Parallax or scroll effects for their own sake. Motion is limited to the type and fields revealing once.
  - Near-black text set on terracotta at body size. It fails contrast and is for display type only.
